facts.text: Dayton moved from a spot 2 miles inland to Flathead Lake’s west shore in 1910, chasing better trade and boating access.
The town’s early economy was built on logging, with timber mills fueling growth through the mid‑20th century.
Dayton’s historic Dayton State Bank, constructed in 1912 in Egyptian Revival style, was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2012.
The first Protestant church on the Flathead Indian Reservation, Dayton Presbyterian Church, was founded in Dayton.
Dayton is home to Montana’s first bonded winery, Mission Mountain Winery, adding a unique wine‑making heritage to the town.
In 1910, famed railroad magnate Cornelius Vanderbilt stayed at the Dayton Hotel, praising it as one of only four truly comfortable places between New York and Seattle.
